project.title: Beilinson–Bloch Heights and the Strong Zero-Curvature Green Conjecture
project.subtitle: Actual Green forms, canonical pairings, and arithmetic finiteness
project.summary: A research programme towards an unconditional Beilinson–Bloch height pairing in arbitrary dimension, centred on the Strong Green conjecture and its conditional local-to-global height theorem.
project.motivation:
Beilinson–Bloch heights extend the arithmetic information carried by heights on curves to homologically trivial cycles in higher codimension. The goal is an unconditional canonical real pairing for complementary rational Chow classes on smooth projective geometrically integral varieties over number fields.

The principal approach is the Strong Green conjecture: construct an actual zero-curvature Green form for each prescribed homologically trivial cycle over the original local field, on its exact support complement and against all compact actual tests. Theorem 7.5 gives the full Chow pairing from Strong G at every finite completion in both complementary codimensions, under the standing analytic and global foundations.

Theorem 2.2 supplies the Chow-invariant actual Bott–Chern obstruction and prescribed curved Green pairs. General vanishing of that obstruction remains open. Alternative approaches include vanishing on localized global classes, admissible arithmetic liftings and cohomological constructions; the Overview links their precise statements and sources.
project.programme: The local construction of the Chow obstruction and prescribed curved actual Green pairs is established. The construction strand now focuses on homological source-image vanishing, numerical certificates and the additional trace or intersection interfaces required by particular height arguments. The properties strand separates curve-visible abelian contributions from the residual Griffiths quotient. Arithmetic regulators, integral lattices and fields of definition provide distinct approaches to Northcott finiteness. A comparison strand relates determinant metrics, local heights and degeneration in families.
